stories.title: Nanoengineered ZnO@Nafion-modified label-free ISFETs immunosensor for ultrasensitive detection of TNF-α
stories.description: Tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) is a major pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune regulation and the pathogenesis of various diseases. In this study, an ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) device with a p-type silicon/silicon dioxide/ZnO nanorod wafer (p-type Si/SiO2/ZnO) and a Si/SiO2/ZnO@Nafion substrate was used for TNF-α detection. Unlike previous ISFET TNF-α sensors that mainly focused on achieving low detection limits, this study presented a controlled, head-to-head comparison of uncoated ZnO nanorods and Nafion-coated ZnO gates on the same p-type Si/SiO2 ISFET platform under identical immunoassay conditions. This approach revealed the trade-off between sensitivity and operational robustness, showing that Nafion improved stability, reproducibility, and anti-fouling behavior. The uncoated ZnO gate showed a lower detection limit (0.509 pg/mL); however, the ZnO@Nafion configuration exhibited a significantly higher stability of 7.46% signal change over 21 days compared with 14.5% for the uncoated ZnO gate. Nafion also improved the reproducibility (RSD 2.064% vs. 2.567%) (n = 5). Therefore, here we present a controlled comparison of ZnO and ZnO@Nafion gate structures on the same ISFET platform, which not only enhances sensitivity but also improves the Nafion surface layer’s operational stability, reproducibility, and anti-fouling behavior. These features confirm the robust performance of the sensor for label-free, real-time clinical analysis of TNF-α, with sensitivity comparable to the gold-standard ELISA method, opening the prospect of replacing traditional, expensive, and time-consuming methods.

stories.title: Enhancing mechanical and physical performance of basalt/nylon fiber metal laminates with SiC nanoparticles
stories.description: This study explores the effect of silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles on both the mechanical and physical characteristics of aluminum-laminated hybrid composites reinforced with basalt and nylon fibers, representing a previously unexplored basalt-nylon hybrid fiber metal laminate system modified with SiC nanoparticles. The composites were made through a hand lay-up process, followed by compression molding and surface lamination with chemically treated aluminum sheets. SiC particles were incorporated at 0, 3, and 5 wt% to optimize the mechanical and physical attributes and to evaluate their influence on tensile strength, flexural strength, impact resistance, and water absorption behavior. The results show that only the highest tensile properties were achieved with 5 wt% SiC (SiC5), but other properties declined. However, 3 wt% SiC (SiC3) provided the best overall performance. Specifically, the tensile strength showed an increase from 117.71 MPa for the control sample (CS) to 121.19 MPa for SiC3, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 3%. In contrast, the flexural strength increased by about 5% in SiC3 and achieved a maximum flexural strength of 173.85 MPa compared to the control sample (CS). Moreover, the tensile and flexural moduli improved significantly by 159% and 46%, respectively, over the unfilled control specimen. A moderate improvement in impact resistance was also observed. Additionally, water absorption decreased by nearly 16% relative to CS, which is likely due to the uniform dispersion of SiC nanoparticles and the resulting improvement in barrier properties. However, a rise in SiC content to 5 wt% caused a decline in flexural strength, impact resistance, and moisture resistance, although the highest tensile strength of 122.3 MPa was achieved at this loading, likely due to particle agglomeration as well as void formation, as confirmed by SEM analysis.

stories.title: Water triggers visible-light photochromism in a hydrogen-bonded organic framework
stories.description: Photochromic materials switched by user-friendly conditions are highly sought after for secure information technologies and adaptive camouflage but remain a formidable challenge. Here, by leveraging dynamic H-bond networks and periodic π-stacked columns in a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF), we report a reversible visible light photochromic system using water as a “trigger” rather than “destroyer”. This behavior arises in a pyrene-based framework, HOF-14, where water adsorption induces a specific lattice contraction via dynamic H-bond network. Such structural change triggers a fundamental redistribution of the framework’s electronic structure, dramatically lowering the exciton binding energy fallen below the ambient thermal energy. This enables spontaneous visible-light-driven electron-hole separation to form pyrene radical cations, which are stabilized by the stacked pyrene columns in HOF. The photochromic transition—a rapid color change from yellow to green within 10 s—is reversible over 50 cycles. We demonstrate high-level information encryption using this HOF ink and its hydrogel formulations, and fabricate adaptive camouflage textiles that dynamically match a foliated environment. These HOF smart textiles are readily recyclable in a closed-loop process, benefiting from the inherent self-repair capability of HOFs—a distinctive feature not found in other classes of porous crystalline materials. Designing photochromic materials which can be switched by user-friendly conditions remains challenging. Here the authors report a reversible visible light photochromic system using water as a trigger rather than destroyer.

stories.title: An extended technology acceptance model for the use of virtual reality in education
stories.description: The present study investigates the use of virtual reality in education through an extended technology acceptance model. This study aims to examine factors that can impact the use of VR in education, expanding its benefits for both students and professors. The model includes six variables: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and continuous usage intention (specific to the traditional acceptance model), to which we added hedonism (pleasure), personality innovativeness as a personality trait and cybersickness as a health concern. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to examine the influence of several variables on the decision to adopt VR technology. Data were gathered from both students and professors who previously used VR headsets in education. The results show that perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and personal innovativeness influence VR usage intention. Hedonism influences both perceived ease of use and usefulness. Surprisingly, cybersickness did not impact the decision to use the VR technology in our study. The findings are helpful for education decision-makers in shaping curricula around new technological advancements and in making the content taught more appealing to younger generations.
